entry.title: CSSPerspective: fix pages and add examples
entry.content:
This updates CSSPerspective, its constructor, and its length property (CSS Typed OM API) to match the spec, and replaces the "To do" stub examples.

  • Fix the API link (it pointed to the CSSOM docs).
  • Add a Description covering what a perspective does, the length values (a <length> or the keyword none), is2D (always false; setting it has no effect), and what toString() and toMatrix() return.
  • Fix length, which said that a value of 0 or a negative number applies no perspective. A length smaller than 1px is treated as 1px, and the keyword none applies no perspective.
  • Add the constructor's return value, and give its parameter type.
  • Add examples to every page, including a live example that changes the perspective of a rotated box.

This covers the CSSPerspective items in the stub list at #28118 (comment)

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • The example output was checked in Chromium, not Firefox.
  • The spec doesn't define any steps for setting length, but Chromium and Firefox convert the string "none" to a CSSKeywordValue and throw a TypeError for other values (as the WPT tests expect). The docs don't mention setter behavior.
  • BCD says Chrome supports CSSPerspective from version 66, but Chrome only accepts none from version 97. BCD has no subfeature for this.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46594

entry.title: FF162 RTCPeerConnection: iceCandidatePoolSize and setConfiguration() fixes
entry.content:
FF162 adds support for iceCandidatePoolSize in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1529398

This updates the RTCPeerConnection() constructor and setConfiguration() pages to match the spec.

  • Rewrite the iceCandidatePoolSize description: it's an integer from 0 to 255 (it said 16-bit), it counts sets of candidates gathered before setLocalDescription(), and pooled candidates use STUN/TURN server resources.
  • Add an Exceptions section to the constructor.
  • Fix setConfiguration()'s InvalidModificationError: list the options that can't be changed, and say that iceCandidatePoolSize can't be changed once setLocalDescription() has been called. Add the TypeError.
  • Fix the certificates notes, which said a changed value is ignored. It throws InvalidModificationError.
  • Change the setConfiguration() example to start from getConfiguration(), and move the intro detail into a Description section.

BCD in mdn/browser-compat-data#31244

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • The exception conditions come from the spec's constructor and "set the configuration" steps, and weren't tested in a browser.
  • The getConfiguration() example adds a certificate by calling setConfiguration(), which the spec says throws InvalidModificationError. That page isn't changed here.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46648

entry.title: Sec-Fetch-Dest: explain values for navigations through a service worker
entry.content:
Description

This PR fixes the document directive on the Sec-Fetch-Dest page.
It no longer says "user-initiated".
It also adds a section about navigations that pass through a service worker.
The FetchEvent page gets a second example, "Opting out of iframe navigations".
The Sec-Fetch-User page gets a short section about the same case.
All three pages link to each other.

Motivation

A document request is not always user-initiated.
User activation is what Sec-Fetch-User reports.

Servers often use Sec-Fetch-Dest: document to detect top-level navigations.
This breaks when a service worker forwards the navigation with event.respondWith(fetch(event.request)).
The new section explains what the server sees in that case and how it tells top-level and iframe navigations apart.
Many service workers only serve and cache top-level navigations.
The FetchEvent example shows how such a service worker opts out of iframe navigations, so they keep Sec-Fetch-Dest: iframe.

Additional details

  • A passthrough fetch sends Sec-Fetch-Dest: empty for top-level navigations and for iframe navigations.
  • Per the Request() constructor, that fetch keeps the mode navigate. The mode changes to same-origin only when init is not empty.
  • The pages describe the spec behavior only. Browser differences are left out.
  • A passthrough fetch does not send Sec-Fetch-User, even after a user click.
  • The WPT test service-workers/service-worker/navigation-headers.https.html expects navigate / empty for passthrough iframe navigations.

Related issues and pull requests

  • Spec discussion: w3c/ServiceWorker#1803
  • Firefox sends same-origin for the passthrough fetch today: Bugzilla 2035038

entry.title: build(deps-dev): bump the npm-dev group with 2 updates
entry.content:
Bumps the npm-dev group with 2 updates: cspell and markdownlint-cli2.

Updates cspell from 10.5.1 to 10.5.2

Release notes

Sourced from cspell's releases.

v10.5.2

Fixes

fix: --gitignore skips nested repositories in ignored folders again (#9648)

Summary

With --gitignore (useGitignore), cspell again skips a git repository kept in a folder that .gitignore excludes, such as a tool's cache of cloned dependencies. Since 10.4.0, these files were checked. A submodule in an ignored folder is still checked, as git does.

Fixes #9645

Before and after

A project with a clone in an ignored cache folder, and a submodule in an ignored vendor/ folder:

project/
  .gitignore     .cache/ and vendor/
  .gitmodules    lists vendor/lib
  README.md
  .cache/dep/    a clone, with its own .git
  vendor/lib/    a submodule

Before, cspell checked the clone:

$ cspell lint --gitignore --dot "**/*.md"
.cache/dep/NOTES.md:1:1 - Unknown word (Thsi) fix: (This)
.cache/dep/NOTES.md:1:9 - Unknown word (misspeled) fix: (misspelled)
vendor/lib/NOTES.md:1:1 - Unknown word (Anothr) fix: (Another)
vendor/lib/NOTES.md:1:8 - Unknown word (typpo) fix: (typo)
CSpell: Files checked: 3, Issues found: 4 in 2 files.

After, it skips the clone and checks the submodule:

$ cspell lint --gitignore --dot "**/*.md"
vendor/lib/NOTES.md:1:1 - Unknown word (Anothr) fix: (Another)
vendor/lib/NOTES.md:1:8 - Unknown word (typpo) fix: (typo)
CSpell: Files checked: 2, Issues found: 2 in 1 file.

What to know:

  • A repository in an ignored folder is skipped with all its files, unless .gitmodules lists it as a submodule.
  • A repository added with plain git add, without a .gitmodules entry, is skipped too.

entry.title: csp default-src: remove outdated firefox svg sprite section
entry.content:
Description

removes the "firefox default-src: none svg sprite blocking issue" section from the default-src page.

Motivation

the section is about a firefox bug that got fixed in firefox 132 (bug 1773976). since then firefox applies img-src to svg <use href> loads like other browsers, so default-src 'none'; img-src 'self' just works and the workaround isn't needed anymore. the page already has a note saying it's fixed, which makes the section confusing to read.

Additional details

i checked it in a current firefox nightly with a small local server:

  • default-src 'none'; img-src 'self': sprite loads and renders
  • default-src 'self'; img-src 'none': sprite is blocked, so img-src is what controls it now
  • default-src 'none': blocked

the engineer who fixed the bug suggested mostly reverting #34592 (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1773976#c15). the other two pages #34592 touched don't have the sprite text anymore, so this was the last bit. nothing else links to the removed anchor.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #36745
Relates to #34592

entry.title: CSSScale: fix pages and add examples
entry.content:
This updates CSSScale, its constructor, and its x, y, and z properties (CSS Typed OM API) to match the spec, and replaces the "To do" stub examples.

  • Fix the API link (it pointed to the CSSOM docs), and say it represents any scaling function, not just scale() and scale3d().
  • Remove text copied from CSSTranslate ("translating vector", and z moving the element towards the viewer), and say what the scale factors do.
  • Fix z, which said that setting it makes is2D false. z defaults to 1, and is2D decides whether it's used.
  • Add a Description covering numbers and CSSNumericValue values, percentages read from CSS, is2D, and toString().
  • Add examples to every page, including a live example that grows a box.

This covers the CSSScale items in the stub list at #28118 (comment)

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • The example output was checked in Chromium, not Firefox.
  • The spec's x, y, and z setters only convert numbers, but Chromium (and the WPT tests) throw a TypeError for non-numbers. The docs don't mention setter checks.
  • The spec writes a 2D scale with equal x and y as scale(x), but Chromium writes scale(x, x). The examples avoid this case.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46594

entry.title: CSSTranslate: fix pages and add examples
entry.content:
This updates CSSTranslate, its constructor, and its x, y, and z properties (CSS Typed OM API) to match the spec, and replaces the "To do" stub examples.

  • Fix the API link (it pointed to the CSSOM docs), and say it represents any translation function, not just translate().
  • Add a Description covering the value types, is2D, and what toString() and toMatrix() return.
  • Give the type of the parameters and properties as a CSSNumericValue (they gave CSS types such as <length-percentage>).
  • Fix z, which said that having a z value makes the transform 3D. z defaults to 0px, and is2D decides whether it's used.
  • Add examples to every page, including a live example that moves a box.

This covers the CSSTranslate items in the stub list at #28118 (comment)

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • The example output was checked in Chromium, not Firefox.
  • The spec doesn't define any checks when setting x, y, or z, but Chromium throws a TypeError for a value of the wrong type. The docs don't mention setter checks.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46594
